transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen, Samira Patel, Jordan Lee, Miguel Torres, Riley Brooks, Taylor Nguyen + all company (approx)

Summary (auto): Quick company health update, product/infra highlights, roadmap and hiring/ops announcements, Q&A.

[00:00] Avery Chen: All right good morning, good afternoon everyone uh thanks for joining the December all hands. Uh we'll kick off, quick housekeeping, recording is on, slides are posted in the invite, and we have a full agenda — company health, infra update, product roadmap, and q&a.

[00:35] Riley Brooks: Quick shoutout — team, closed three net-new enterprise deals this month, great work, really helped our December metrics.

[01:12] Avery Chen: Nice, yeah huge thanks. Topline first: revenue and usage — we finished Q4 pacing ahead of plan, ARR growth is healthy, retention is stable. There s also been a big uptick in Dedicated inquiries, and Private deployments coming through in pipeline. Noting: these are early signals not contractual closes yet.

[02:05] Jordan Lee: I'll cover infra — we've pushed a runtime release that improves batching and lowers tail latency by about 12% in our internal benchmarks, this included new kernel selection heuristics and better kv cache handling — some of the transcriptions might say K V cash, but it's KV cache. We've also stabilized autoscaler for Dedicated pools; edge cases remain for tiny bursty workloads where cold-starts can still be painful. We're working on a warm pool approach to reduce cold starts.

[03:40] Samira Patel: Engineering highlights — shipped streaming function-calls for hosted API, rolled out a set of quantization profiles that reduce token cost for many LLMs without noticeable quality regressions in our evals. We started an internal pilot for model switcher: routing policy by latency/cost tier. There were a few bugs in the initial rollout, QA caught some regressions in structured output that we fixed yesterday.

[05:10] Miguel Torres: Product — big focus for Q1 is three things: 1) Redwood Optimize — a first-party tool to recommend batching/quantization/cache settings per-route; 2) Rollouts — improve canary and A/B tooling for model rollouts; 3) Private installer improvements for on-prem and VPC ease-of-use. We'll publish the draft Q1 roadmap next month.

[06:02] Avery Chen: On security/compliance we have a status update — SOC 2 readiness is in progress, most controls are mapped, we have external assessor onboarding next week. Audit logs and KMS integrations are being prioritized for Private customers. Note: this is a company priority for enterprise deals.

[06:45] Taylor Nguyen: People ops update — hiring pause for non-engineering ICs for next 30 days to shore up budget assumptions. Engineering and sales hires continue in prioritized areas. We re also rolling out manager training on performance conversations and calibration. Holiday PTO guidelines coming later today.

[08:00] Riley Brooks: Sales motion — churn is low, expansion is main lever; we re focusing on POC to Dedicated conversion playbooks and a faster security pack for procurement teams. Also have a partnership with CloudVendorX to simplify private-region deployments, still in pilot.

[09:10] Audience question (Employee): Any plans to change pricing?

[09:22] Avery Chen: No immediate pricing changes. We re exploring packaging adjustments for Dedicated and Private to improve predictability for customers, but nothing to announce.

[10:00] Jordan Lee: Technical deep dive snippet — noticed confusion around our cache invalidation semantics when using prefix caching + model variants; engineering will publish a simple d0c and run a tech notes session next week to explain expected behaviors.

[11:18] Samira Patel: On quality and evals — we re formalizing regression detection tied to prompt sets. Product e2e tests now include a sample of customer prompts (anonymized) to detect quality drift when we push new runtimes or quantization profiles.

[12:05] Miguel Torres: Roadmap specifics — feature prioritization rationale: customer demand + unit econ impact. For Q1 we're prioritizing Optimize and Rollouts, then Private UX improvements. Smaller items: embedding batching API and improved tracing hooks for observability.

[13:30] Audience question (Engineering): What's the plan for open models vs our curated catalog?

[13:45] Samira Patel: We'll keep a curated set of models we verify for perf and quality; the catalog will show recommended quantization & kernel profiles. We'll also allow customers to bring their own models in Private mode, but we will not 'bless' every community model without vetting.

[15:00] Avery Chen: Hiring and org changes — small leadership tweak: Riley will now lead GTM ops and interactions with Solution Architects to tighten the POC to commit path. We're also creating a Senior Engineering Manager role focused on inference runtime stability — hiring immediate.

[16:10] Taylor Nguyen: Compensation cycle reminder — review meetings to managers scheduled next week, calibration in two weeks. If you have questions reach out to People Ops.

[17:00] Audience question: Any layoffs or org reductions?

[17:12] Avery Chen: No broad layoffs. We're tightening spending and paused some hiring as Taylor noted; decisions are targeted. We re prioritizing doubling down on product lines that drive revenue (Dedicated, Private, Optimize).

[18:00] Jordan Lee: Ops note — region availability updates: new APAC region launch is on track for early Q1; couple of compliance certs pending (data residency paperwork). We'll post a region availability calendar.

[19:20] Riley Brooks: On customer success — CS pilot for Dedicated customers helped lower time-to-value by 30%, we re scaling that play. Also improving onboarding templates and security pack for procurement.

[20:05] Audience question (Sales): How do we handle benchmarking requests?

[20:20] Miguel Torres: We have a benchmark spreadsheet and template for customers, we'll include a short-run script and guidance. For enterprise benchmarks we recommend Dedicated or Private pilot; we'll share a link in the follow up.

[21:30] Avery Chen: Financials — high level: burn rate decreased slightly due to ops improvements, runway extends into mid-2027 under current plan. We're aiming to get to breakeven on unit economics for core hosted flows by next year, via batching/quantization gains and better routing to lower-cost model variants.

[22:40] Audience question (Product): What success metrics should teams track?

[22:55] Miguel Torres: Track three metrics by route: latency P95, cost per token (unit econ), and quality (measured by evals + customer-reported regressions). We'll create a dashboard template in Console.

[24:10] Samira Patel: Engineering OKRs — focus on reliability (SLO uptime), performance (latency improvements), and developer productivity (deploy pipeline, fewer rollbacks).

[25:00] Audience question (Legal): Procurement asks about data retention and customer logs — what's the policy?

[25:15] Avery Chen: Default retention for hosted is 30 days; Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention and opt-in long-term logs with KMS. Legal and Security will publish a concise FAQ and a security pack for procurement.

[26:20] Quick shoutouts: hiring referrals, promotion announcements, and customer wins.

[28:10] Q&A rapid fire — misc questions about remote work policy, expense approvals, and internal tooling timelines.

[34:30] Deep question about reliability during peak retail events — Jordan: we re improving graceful degradation and multi-tier fallback: model variants, regional fallback, and reserve Dedicated capacity. We'll simulate main events in chaos testing.

[40:00] Avery Chen: Closing remarks — thanks for the fast quarter, the focus is on converting POCs to Dedicated, shipping Optimize, and getting SOC 2 done. We'll follow up with slides, recording and action items.

[41:00] Quick recap of next steps by Miguel and Samira, and call ended after a short team sync for leadership to discuss follow-ups.

Notes: transcript contains typical auto-transcription artifacts (misheard acronyms, punctuation). Links referenced in meeting: slides (docs.redwood.ai/allhands/2026-12), benchmark sheet (sheets.redwood.ai/benchmarks/dec-2026), SOC2 tracker (internal.redwood.ai/security/soc2).
